diameter_m.why: base corner to base corner: the repository's reference 3V panel dome (panel_method.CONSTANTS base_ft, 16 ft)

stick_w_m.why: a stick's width flat on the jig: half a 2x3's 2-1/2 in, less the kerf. The rip that halves the 2x3 is the bevel itself, so it runs through the board's thickness, not across it

stick_d_m.why: a stick's depth through the wall: the 2x3's 1-1/2 in thickness, which the bevelled rip face spans

base_h_m.why: base board height under the lowest base corner: a 2x6 on edge (panel_method)

plate_w_m.why: bottom plate width: a pressure-treated 2x4 laid flat

riser_m.why: pony wall under the base sections: none on the reference dome

door_w_m.why: clear door opening: a 32 in leaf's opening, the narrowest an accessible door allows

door_h_m.why: clear door opening height: 6 ft 4 in, a standard leaf

door_h_min_m.why: the lowest clear opening accepted when the head is moved to a panel corner: small domes commonly take a 6 ft door

door_gap_m.why: gap round the leaf for hinges and swelling

post_w_m.why: door post across the opening: a 2x4's thickness

post_d_m.why: door post through the wall: a 2x4's width

head_h_m.why: door head depth: a 2x4 on edge

card_t_m.why: door cards: 3/4 in plywood fins between the posts and the skin

skin_t_m.why: panel skin: 1/2 in plywood under shingles (cabin), or twin-wall polycarbonate (clear)

board_l_m.why: 2x3 stock length: 8 ft studs, each ripped into two sticks

trim_m.why: extra length cut on every stick before its final mitre

deck_h_m.why: deck top above the ground: piers and joists under it

deck_front_m.why: the porch in front of the door

porch_w_m.why: porch width across the door: room for two chairs either side of the path

deck_board_m.why: decking pitch: a 5/4x6 board (5-1/2 in) and its gap

screws_per_corner.why: 75 mm screws through each panel corner joint

seam_screw_m.why: panel-to-panel screw spacing along a seam

staple_m.why: staple spacing round a skinned section

waste.why: allowance on sheet goods and tape for offcuts and mistakes

person_m.why: the figure standing beside the dome for scale
